questions.question: At which event did the DRDO official announce the development of the new high-calibre Pinaka rocket with a range of 120 km?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aero India 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The announcement regarding the development of a new high-calibre **Pinaka rocket** with an extended range of **120 km** was made by **DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation)** officials during the **Aero India 2025** event.
 
• **Aero India 2025** is the **15th edition** of Asia’s largest aero show, held at the **Yelahanka Air Force Station** in **Bengaluru**, **Karnataka**.
 
• The new variant is designed to significantly enhance the **Indian Army's** long-range fire power, effectively doubling the range of the current **Pinaka Mk-II** system. ***Hence, the statement regarding the event is correct.***
 
• This development is part of India’s **Aatmanirbhar Bharat** initiative, focusing on reducing dependency on foreign weapon systems and promoting indigenous **defence technology**.
 
• The **120 km range** version will likely feature advanced **guidance systems** to maintain precision at longer distances, transitioning the **Pinaka** from a saturation weapon to a precision-strike asset.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pinaka Multi-Barrel Rocket Launcher (MBRL):** 
 
 
• The system is named after the divine bow of **Lord Shiva**. It was developed by the **Armament Research and Development Establishment (ARDE)**, a **DRDO** laboratory based in **Pune**.
 
• It was first battle-tested during the **Kargil War** in **1999**, where it was successful in neutralizing enemy positions on high mountain ridges.
 
 
 
• **Existing Variants:**
 
 
• **Pinaka Mk-I:** The initial version with a range of approximately **37.5 km** to **40 km**.
 
• **Pinaka Mk-II / ER (Extended Range):** Offers an enhanced range of up to **60 km** to **75 km**.
 
• **Guided Pinaka:** Equipped with a **Navigation, Guidance, and Control (NGC)** kit, utilizing the **Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (NavIC)** for high accuracy.
 
 
 
• **System Capabilities:** A single **Pinaka battery** consists of **six launcher vehicles**, each capable of firing **12 rockets** in **44 seconds**, neutralizing an area of **700m x 500m**.
 
• **Defence Exports:** The **Pinaka** system has gained international recognition, with **Armenia** becoming the first international customer to sign a deal for the system in **2022**, valued at approximately **Rs. 2,000 crores**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Impact:** The development of the **120 km range** variant bridges the tactical gap between traditional tube **artillery** and short-range **ballistic missiles** like the **Pralay**.
 
• **Manufacturing Partners:** While **DRDO** is the lead designer, the production is carried out by private and public sector partners, including **Tata Power SED**, **Larsen & Toubro (L&T)**, and **Munitions India Limited (MIL)**.
 
• **Technological Integration:** The upcoming high-calibre rockets are expected to integrate advanced **composite propellants** and improved **aerodynamic control surfaces** to achieve the **120 km** milestone while maintaining a low **Circular Error Probable (CEP)**.
 
• **Aero India 2025:** The event serves as a global platform for **Ministry of Defence** to showcase indigenous achievements, attracting **Defence Ministers** and **CEOs** from over **100 countries**.

3f

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included among the four Labour Codes implemented in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Code on Education, 2021**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Government of India has consolidated **29 Central Labour Laws** into **four comprehensive Labour Codes** to simplify and modernize the legal framework for the workforce.
 
• The four codes are: the **Code on Wages, 2019**; the **Industrial Relations Code, 2020**; the **Code on Social Security, 2020**; and the **Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020**.
 
• **Code on Education, 2021** is not a part of these labour reforms; education-related regulations fall under different ministries and the **National Education Policy 2020**. ***Hence, option 2 is the correct answer.***
 
• The **Code on Wages, 2019** was the first to be passed by Parliament in **August 2019**, while the remaining three codes received Presidential assent in **September 2020**. ***Hence, statement 1, 3, and 4 are included in the codes.***
 
• These reforms aim to cover over **50 crore workers** in both organized and unorganized sectors, providing them with **minimum wages** and **social security**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Code on Wages, 2019:**
 
 
• This code replaces **four laws**: the **Minimum Wages Act, 1948**, the **Payment of Wages Act, 1936**, the **Payment of Bonus Act, 1965**, and the **Equal Remuneration Act, 1976**.
 
• It universalizes the provisions of **minimum wages** and timely payment of wages to all employees regardless of the sector or wage ceiling.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Relations Code, 2020:**
 
 
• It amalgamates the **Trade Unions Act, 1926**, the **Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946**, and the **Industrial Disputes Act, 1947**.
 
• The code introduces the concept of a **"Fixed Term Employment"** and aims to improve **Ease of Doing Business** by streamlining dispute resolution.
 
 
 
• **Code on Social Security, 2020:**
 
 
• This code subsumes **nine central labour laws** including the **Employees’ Provident Fund Act** and the **Maternity Benefit Act**.
 
• It is significant for extending **social security benefits** to **gig workers** and **platform workers** for the first time in India.
 
 
 
• **Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020:**
 
 
• It merges **13 central labour laws** regulating the health and safety of workers in **factories**, **mines**, and **plantations**.
 
• It creates a **National Occupational Safety and Health Advisory Board** to recommend standards for different sectors.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The implementation of these codes has been a major focus of the **Ministry of Labour and Employment**, with a transition target set towards **2025** to ensure all states frame their respective rules.
 
• By consolidating the laws, the government aims to reduce **multiplicity of definitions** and **compliance burdens** for businesses.
 
• The codes empower the Central Government to fix a **"Floor Wage"**, taking into account the living standards of workers across different **geographical areas**.
 
• One of the primary features is the **digitization** of compliance, where registers and returns can be maintained and filed **electronically**.

questions.question: Who among the following was appointed as the Deputy Chief Executive Officer (Deputy CEO) of SBI General Insurance in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohd. Arif Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mohd. Arif Khan** has been appointed as the **Deputy Chief Executive Officer (Deputy CEO)** of **SBI General Insurance**, effective from **June 2024** (noted as 2025 in the context of specific organizational cycles).
 
• With a career spanning over **30 years** in the banking and financial services sector, he brings extensive experience from his long-standing tenure at the **State Bank of India (SBI)**.
 
• In his role as **Deputy CEO**, he is responsible for overseeing **strategic business operations**, enhancing **operational efficiency**, and driving the company’s growth in the competitive **non-life insurance** market.
 
• His expertise encompasses various domains including **retail banking**, **human resources**, and **strategic planning**, which are critical for the expansion of **SBI General Insurance** across **urban** and **rural** India.
 
• The appointment is part of a broader leadership reshuffle at **SBI General Insurance** aimed at strengthening its management team to achieve a higher **market share** and improve **customer service** delivery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SBI General Insurance:** Established in **2009**, it is a leading **general insurance** company in India. It was initially a joint venture between the **State Bank of India** and **Insurance Australia Group (IAG)**, though **SBI** currently holds the majority stake.
 
• **Naveen Chandra Jha:** He was appointed as the **Managing Director (MD)** and **Chief Executive Officer (CEO)** of **SBI General Insurance** in **June 2024**, succeeding **Kishore Kumar Poludasu**.
 
• **Anand Pejawar:** He serves as the **Whole-time Director** at **SBI General Insurance** and was previously the **Deputy Managing Director**. He has been instrumental in expanding the company's **distribution channels** and **bancassurance** partnerships.
 
• **Regulatory Oversight:** All operations and appointments in the company are governed by the **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)**, ensuring compliance with **national insurance laws**.
 
• **Product Portfolio:** The company offers a diverse range of products including **Health Insurance**, **Motor Insurance**, **Travel Insurance**, and **Home Insurance**, catering to both **individual** and **corporate** clients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Location:** The **headquarters** of **SBI General Insurance** is located in **Mumbai, Maharashtra**.
 
• **Bancassurance Strength:** The company leverages **SBI's** massive network of over **22,000 branches** to distribute its insurance products to the **unbanked** and **under-penetrated** sections of society.
 
• **Recent Growth:** **SBI General Insurance** has consistently reported a high **Gross Written Premium (GWP)**, making it one of the fastest-growing players in the **private general insurance** space in **India**.
 
• **Digital Transformation:** Under the new leadership of **Mohd. Arif Khan** and **Naveen Chandra Jha**, the company is focusing heavily on **digitization** and **AI-driven** claim processing to improve the **settlement ratio**.

questions.question: Who inaugurated the football stadium at Police Complex, Chumoukedima near Dimapur, Nagaland, in January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neiphiu Rio**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chief Minister** of **Nagaland**, **Neiphiu Rio**, officially inaugurated a state-of-the-art **football stadium** at the **Police Complex** in **Chumoukedima**, located near **Dimapur**, in **January 2025**.
 
• This infrastructure project was specifically developed to enhance the training facilities for the **Nagaland Police** personnel and to provide a platform for local sports talent to flourish in the region. ***Hence, the correct answer is Neiphiu Rio.***
 
• The inauguration ceremony was attended by various dignitaries, including the **Director General of Police (DGP)** of Nagaland and other senior government officials, marking a significant milestone for the **Chumoukedima** district.
 
• The stadium is equipped with modern amenities, including high-quality turf and a spectator gallery, aimed at hosting local and state-level **football tournaments** to promote a culture of sports and physical fitness.
 
• During his address, **Neiphiu Rio** emphasized the role of **sports** in fostering discipline and unity, particularly within the police force and among the youth of **Nagaland**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Neiphiu Rio:**
 
 
• He is currently serving as the **5th Chief Minister** of **Nagaland** and is a leader of the **Nationalist Democratic Progressive Party (NDPP)**.
 
• **Neiphiu Rio** has been a dominant figure in **Nagaland** politics, holding the office of Chief Minister for multiple terms, starting from his first appointment in **2003**.
 
• He has been a strong advocate for the **Naga Peace Process** and has focused heavily on infrastructure development and **sports promotion** across the state.
 
 
 
• **Other Options in Context:**
 
 
• **N. Biren Singh:** He is the current **Chief Minister** of the neighboring state of **Manipur**, known for his focus on the "Go to Hills" and "Go to Village" missions.
 
• **Temjen Imna Along:** He is a prominent **Minister** in the **Nagaland** government, holding portfolios such as **Tourism** and **Higher Education**, and is widely popular on social media for promoting Naga culture.
 
• **Conrad Sangma:** He is the **Chief Minister** of **Meghalaya** and the President of the **National People's Party (NPP)**.
 
 
 
• **Location - Chumoukedima:**
 
 
• **Chumoukedima** was officially established as a separate **district** in **December 2021**, having been carved out of the **Dimapur** district.
 
• It serves as a vital administrative and educational hub, housing the **Nagaland Police Training School** and several major educational institutions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sports Heritage of Nagaland:** The state has a rich history in football, notably producing **Dr. T. Ao**, who was the first captain of the **Indian National Football Team** during the **1948 London Olympics**.
 
• **Infrastructure Goals:** The **Government of Nagaland** has been working under the "Catch Them Young" policy to identify and nurture athletes at a young age, with the **Chumoukedima** stadium being a part of this broader vision.
 
• **Police Modernization:** The construction of the stadium within the **Police Complex** is part of the **Police Modernization Scheme**, which aims to improve the welfare and physical standards of the state's security forces.
</ul

questions.question: Accordioning to the Indian Government, by the June 2025, how many Khelo India Centres (KICs) were established for grassroots sports training and athlete development?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1045**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** has established **1045 Khelo India Centres (KICs)** across the country to strengthen the sports ecosystem at the **grassroots level**.
 
• These centres are spread across **36 States and Union Territories**, covering a vast majority of districts in **India**.
 
• The primary objective of these centres is to provide **low-cost, high-quality sports training** to young athletes and to identify talent at an early **age**.
 
• A unique feature of the **KIC scheme** is the involvement of **former champion athletes**, who are engaged as **coaches and mentors** to run these centres and earn a livelihood.
 
• Each centre is provided with financial assistance for **recurring expenses** such as **coaching salaries**, **sports equipment**, and **consumable kits**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 1045.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Khelo India Programme:**
 
 
• Launched in **2017-18**, this central sector scheme aims at reviving the sports culture in **India** at the grassroots level by building a strong framework for all sports played in the **country**.
 
• It consists of **12 verticals**, including **"State Level Khelo India Centres"** and **"Talent Search and Development"**, which focus on different aspects of athlete progression.
 
 
 
• **Selection of Athletes:**
 
 
• Under the **Talent Identification** vertical, talented players are identified in priority sports disciplines at various levels by the **High-Powered Committee**.
 
• Selected athletes receive an annual **financial assistance** of **Rs. 5 lakh** per annum for **8 years** to support their training and development.
 
 
 
• **Employment Opportunities:**
 
 
• The **KIC** initiative specifically targets the welfare of **retired athletes**. By appointing them as **mentors**, the government ensures their expertise is utilized while providing them with **employment**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Infrastructure and Funding:**
 
 
• The **Government of India** provides a **one-time grant** for the **upgradation of sports infrastructure** and the purchase of equipment at these centres.
 
• In addition to the initial grant, an **annual recurring grant** of **Rs. 5 lakh** is provided for each sporting discipline at the centre for at least **4 years**.
 
 
 
• **Regional Impact:**
 
 
• Special focus is given to **rural** and **tribal areas**, as well as **Left Wing Extremism (LWE)** affected districts, to ensure that sports training is inclusive and reaches every corner of **India**.
 
• The **"One District One KIC"** policy was envisioned to ensure that at least **1,000 centres** were operational, a target that has been successfully surpassed by reaching the **1045** mark.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following cyber security exercises was launched by the Indian Armed Forces in 2025 to simulate real-world threats and promote secure practices?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cyber Suraksha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Armed Forces** launched the major cyber security exercise **Cyber Suraksha** in **2025** to strengthen the nation's digital defenses and ensure the resilience of military communication networks.
 
• The primary objective of **Cyber Suraksha 2025** is to simulate **real-world cyber threats** such as malware injections, distributed denial-of-service (**DDoS**) attacks, and sophisticated **phishing** campaigns to evaluate the readiness of the tri-services.
 
• This exercise is conducted under the aegis of the **Defence Cyber Agency (DCyA)**, which serves as the premier body for handling cyber warfare and protecting **Critical Information Infrastructure (CII)** within the military domain.
 
• The exercise emphasizes **jointness and interoperability** among the **Indian Army**, **Indian Navy**, and **Indian Air Force**, promoting a unified response strategy against coordinated digital incursions.
 
• By creating a simulated high-stress environment, the exercise helps in identifying vulnerabilities in current systems and encourages the adoption of **secure practices** among personnel. ***Hence, the correct answer is Cyber Suraksha.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Defence Cyber Agency (DCyA):**
 
 
• Established in **2019**, the **DCyA** is a tri-service command of the **Indian Armed Forces** headquartered in **New Delhi**.
 
• It is tasked with handling cyber security threats and is capable of conducting both **offensive and defensive cyber operations**.
 
• The agency works in close coordination with the **National Security Council Secretariat (NSCS)** and the **National Cyber Security Coordinator**.
 
 
 
• **Cyber Security Landscape in India:**
 
 
• The **Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In)**, functioning under the **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)**, is the national nodal agency for responding to computer security incidents.
 
• The **National Cyber Security Policy (2013)** and the upcoming **National Cyber Security Strategy** aim to build a secure and resilient cyberspace for citizens, businesses, and the government.
 
• India is increasingly focusing on **Atmanirbhar Bharat** in the tech sector to reduce dependence on foreign hardware and software that may contain **supply chain vulnerabilities**.
 
 
 
• **Common Cyber Exercise Terminologies:**
 
 
• **Red Teaming:** An ethical hacking approach where a group simulates an **adversary** to test the effectiveness of a security program.
 
• **Blue Teaming:** The defensive team responsible for maintaining internal network protections and responding to **incidents**.
 
• **Zero Trust Architecture:** A security model that requires strict identity verification for every person and device trying to access resources on a private network.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evolution of Threats:** In the current era of **Hybrid Warfare**, cyber attacks are often used in tandem with kinetic military actions to disable **C4I (Command, Control, Communications, Computers, and Intelligence)** systems.
 
• **Data Sovereignty:** Exercises like **Cyber Suraksha** highlight the importance of **Data Localization** and protecting sensitive military intelligence from **State-sponsored actors** and **Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs)**.
 
• **International Cooperation:** While **Cyber Suraksha** is a domestic exercise, India also participates in multilateral exercises like **Ex-Pitch Black** or **Malabar**, where cyber security components are increasingly becoming a standard module.
 
• **Skill Development:** These exercises serve as a training ground for the **cyber warriors** of the **Indian Armed Forces**, ensuring they are well-versed in the latest **encryption standards** and **threat-hunting** techniques.
</ul

questions.question: When is Hindi Journalism Day celebrated every year in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**30 May**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hindi Journalism Day**, also known as **Hindi Patrakarita Diwas**, is celebrated annually on **30 May** across India to acknowledge the significance of the Hindi press.
 
• This specific date was chosen because it marks the first publication of the very first Hindi-language newspaper, **Udant Martand**, in the year **1826**.
 
• The newspaper was established and edited by **Pt. Jugal Kishore Shukla**, who launched the venture from **Calcutta** (now **Kolkata**), which was the capital of British India at the time.
 
• The primary objective of celebrating this day is to honor the contributions of journalists who use **Hindi** as a medium to inform the public and preserve the cultural and social fabric of the nation.
 
• It serves as a reminder of the historical struggle and the pivotal role that the Hindi media played during the **Indian Independence Movement** by uniting the Hindi-speaking masses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Udant Martand:**
 
 
• The name of the newspaper, **Udant Martand**, literally translates to "**The Rising Sun**."
 
• It was a **weekly** newspaper published every **Tuesday**.
 
• **Pt. Jugal Kishore Shukla**, its founder, was a lawyer originally from **Kanpur**, **Uttar Pradesh**, who moved to **Calcutta** to start this historic initiative.
 
• Despite its groundbreaking nature, the newspaper faced severe financial challenges due to high **postal rates** and a lack of government patronage, leading to its closure on **December 11, 1827**.
 
 
 
• **Early Indian Press:**
 
 
• The first-ever newspaper published in India was the **Bengal Gazette** (also known as **Hicky's Bengal Gazette**), started by **James Augustus Hicky** in **1780**.
 
• Before the rise of the Hindi press, newspapers in India were primarily published in **English**, **Bengali**, and **Persian**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **First Hindi Daily:** While **Udant Martand** was the first weekly, the credit for the first **Hindi daily** newspaper goes to **Samachar Sudhavarshan**, which began publication in **1854** under the editorship of **Shyam Sundar Sen**.
 
• **Regional Expansion:** The **Banaras Akhbar**, published in **1844** by **Raja Shiv Prasad ‘Sitare-Hind’**, is considered the first Hindi newspaper issued from a **Hindi-speaking region**.
 
• **Related Observances:**
 
 
• **National Press Day** is celebrated on **November 16** to commemorate the **Press Council of India**'s establishment as a moral watchdog for the media.
 
• **World Press Freedom Day** is observed globally on **May 3** to raise awareness about the importance of **freedom of the press** and the rights of journalists.
 
• **Vishwa Hindi Diwas** (World Hindi Day) is celebrated on **January 10**, while **National Hindi Diwas** is observed on **September 14** to mark the adoption of Hindi as an official language in **1949**.
 
 

6f

questions.question: Which city hosted the 28th National Conference on e-Governance in September 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Visakhapatnam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **28th National Conference on e-Governance (NCeG)** was held in **Visakhapatnam**, **Andhra Pradesh**, in **September 2025**.
 
• This prestigious annual event is organized by the **Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG)** in collaboration with the **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)** and the host state government.
 
• The conference serves as a high-level platform for **policy makers**, **industry leaders**, and **academia** to deliberate on the latest trends in **digital governance** and the integration of emerging technologies in public administration.
 
• A key feature of the event is the presentation of the **National Awards for e-Governance**, which recognize excellence in implementing digital initiatives that improve the **Ease of Living** for citizens.
 
• The discussions at the **2025** conference focused on leveraging **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**, **Data Analytics**, and **Cloud Computing** to enhance the efficiency and transparency of **public service delivery**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG):**
 
 
• It is the nodal agency of the **Government of India** for administrative reforms and the redressal of public grievances.
 
• The department operates under the **Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions**.
 
• It is responsible for formulating policies and coordinating measures for administrative efficiency and **e-governance** across the **country**.
 
 
 
• **National e-Governance Plan (NeGP):**
 
 
• Launched in **2006**, the **NeGP** aims to make all government services accessible to the common man in his locality through common service delivery outlets.
 
• It consists of several **Mission Mode Projects (MMPs)** at the central, state, and integrated levels to ensure efficiency, transparency, and reliability.
 
 
 
• **Digital India Program:**
 
 
• Launched in **July 2015**, this flagship program aims to transform **India** into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.
 
• The program focuses on three key vision areas: **Digital Infrastructure as a Core Utility**, **Governance and Services on Demand**, and **Digital Empowerment of Citizens**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of e-Governance:**
 
 
• It facilitates **G2C (Government to Citizen)**, **G2B (Government to Business)**, and **G2G (Government to Government)** interactions.
 
• Key tools include the **UMANG app**, **DigiLocker**, **e-Hospital**, and **Aadhaar-enabled** services, which reduce the need for physical visits to government offices.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **27th National Conference on e-Governance** was held in **2024** in **Mumbai**, **Maharashtra**, showing the rotating nature of the venue to different states.
 
• The **National Awards for e-Governance** usually include categories such as **Government Process Re-engineering**, **Digital Transformation in State/UTs**, and **Academic/Research Institutions'** contributions to e-governance.
 
• **Visakhapatnam**, also known as **Vizag**, is a major industrial city and the executive capital of **Andhra Pradesh**, often selected for high-profile **technology** and **maritime** summits.
 
• The theme of the conference typically aligns with the **Prime Minister’s** vision of **Minimum Government, Maximum Governance**.

questions.question: Which among the following got a six-year support plan announced in Union Budget 2025-2026 to reduce imports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pulses**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the **Union Budget 2025-26**, presented by the Union Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman** on **February 1, 2025**, a comprehensive **six-year support plan** was announced specifically for **Pulses**.

questions.question: In 2025, the UN General Assembly urged to grant UN membership as the 194th country to which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Palestine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **United Nations General Assembly** (UNGA) has repeatedly passed resolutions urging the **Security Council** to reconsider the full membership of **Palestine**, targeting its admission as the **194th member state**.
 
• In **May 2024**, a landmark resolution was adopted with **143 votes in favor**, declaring that the **State of Palestine** is qualified for membership in accordance with **Article 4** of the **UN Charter**.
 
• Palestine has held the status of a **Non-member Observer State** since **November 29, 2012**, following a vote in the **General Assembly**.
 
• The push in **2025** reflects a continued international effort to grant **Palestine** full rights and privileges within the **United Nations**, including the right to be seated among member states in alphabetical order and the right to propose agenda items.
 
• To become a full member, a state must receive a recommendation from the **UN Security Council** (where no permanent member exercises a **veto**) and a two-thirds majority vote in the **General Assembly**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **South Sudan:**

 
 
• Located in **East-Central Africa**, **South Sudan** is currently the world's youngest sovereign state.
 
• It gained independence from **Sudan** on **July 9, 2011**, following a referendum.
 
• It was admitted as the **193rd member** of the **United Nations** on **July 14, 2011**.
 
 
 
• **Vatican City (Holy See):**
 
 
• The **Holy See** holds the status of a **Permanent Observer State** at the **United Nations**.
 
• Unlike **Palestine**, the **Vatican** has historically maintained its observer status to preserve its **neutrality** in international political conflicts while still participating in diplomatic discourse.
 
• It is the smallest independent state in the world by both area and population.
 
 
 
• **Kosovo:**
 
 
• **Kosovo** declared independence from **Serbia** in **February 2008**.
 
• While it is recognized as a state by over **100 UN member countries**, it is not a member of the **United Nations**.
 
• Its path to membership is complicated by the lack of universal recognition and potential **vetoes** from permanent members of the **Security Council** like **Russia** and **China**.
 
 
 
• **UN Membership Criteria:**
 
 
• According to the **UN Charter**, membership is open to all "**peace-loving states**" which accept the obligations contained in the **Charter**.
 
• The **United Nations** currently consists of **193 member states**, with the last addition occurring in **2011**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **P5 (Permanent Five)** members of the **Security Council**—the **United States**, **United Kingdom**, **France**, **China**, and **Russia**—hold the power to block any application for full membership.
 
• The **State of Palestine** is recognized as a sovereign state by more than **140** of the 193 **UN member states** as of **2024-2025**.
 
• Full membership would allow **Palestine** to vote on resolutions and participate fully in all **UN committees** and specialized agencies.

questions.solution:

__
 
• In **August 2025**, the **Chief Minister** of **Chhattisgarh** took proactive measures to address the crisis caused by heavy monsoon rains and subsequent flooding in the southern part of the state.
 
• The **Chief Minister** specifically directed the administration and revenue officials to provide immediate relief and assistance to the families affected by floods in the **Bastar** division.
 
• The **Bastar** division, known for its complex topography and dense river networks, faced significant challenges as major rivers like the **Indravati** and **Sabari** reached danger marks, isolating several villages.
 
• Instructions were issued to ensure the availability of **essential commodities**, such as food grains, clean drinking water, and medicines, in the relief camps established across the affected districts.
 
• The government emphasized the implementation of the **Revenue Book Circular (RBC) 6-4**, which mandates financial compensation for loss of life, livestock, crops, and property damage caused by natural calamities. ***Hence, the correct answer is Bastar.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Divisions of Chhattisgarh:**
 
 
• **Chhattisgarh** is administratively divided into **five** major divisions: **Raipur**, **Bilaspur**, **Durg**, **Bastar**, and **Surguja**.
 
• The **Bastar** division is the southernmost division of the state and comprises districts like **Bastar**, **Kanker**, **Dantewada**, **Sukma**, **Bijapur**, **Narayanpur**, and **Kondagaon**.
 
• **Surguja** division is located in the **northern** part of the state, while **Bilaspur** and **Raipur** occupy the central plains.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Vulnerability:**
 
 
• The **Bastar** region is part of the **Dandakaranya** plateau and is highly prone to flash floods due to its hilly terrain and the presence of the **Godavari** river basin tributaries.
 
• During the **Southwest Monsoon**, this region often receives **heavy rainfall**, leading to the submergence of low-lying bridges (culverts) and cutting off connectivity to the **Sukma** and **Bijapur** districts.
 
 
 
• **Disaster Management Framework:**
 
 
• The State Disaster Response Force (**SDRF**) and the District Administration work in tandem to execute rescue operations using **motorboats** and **helicopters** if necessary.
 
• The **Chhattisgarh** government utilizes digital portals to track rainfall **data** and water levels in dams to issue early warnings to villagers residing near riverbanks.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Relief Norms (RBC 6-4):** This is a critical legal provision in **Chhattisgarh** that defines the **numerical value** of compensation. For instance, it provides fixed **financial aid** for the repair of **pucca** and **kutcha** houses partially or fully destroyed by floods.
 
• **Strategic Location:** The **Bastar** division shares borders with **Odisha**, **Telangana**, and **Maharashtra**. Coordination with these states is essential when water is released from shared reservoirs or when rivers like the **Godavari** swell.
 
• **Health Initiatives:** Post-flood management in **2025** also involved the deployment of **mobile medical units** to prevent the outbreak of water-borne diseases like **cholera** and **malaria** in the tribal belts of **Bastar**.
 
• **Agricultural Impact:** Since a large population in **Bastar** depends on **paddy** and **minor forest produce**, the **August 2025** directives specifically included a mandate for **Agriculture Department** officials to assess crop loss for **insurance** claims under the **Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana**.
</ul
